name: Shared rings and distant light flashes: Thomas, then burst-firing, 6 min each (Dotta 2011)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Dotta, Buckner, Lafrenie & Persinger 2011), shared circumcerebral rings
summary: The magnetic half of Dotta, Buckner, Lafrenie & Persinger 2011: two people 10 m apart wear identical eight-coil rings driven by one computer and receive the Thomas pattern, then the burst-firing pattern, 6 min each, while one of them sits in a room lit by 1 to 7 Hz flashes. The paper reports a small rise in photon counts 15 cm from the right side of the other, blindfolded partner's head during burst-firing (3 pairs).
notes: Dotta 2011: the Thomas pattern (the 'primer') ran for the first 6 min and burst-firing for the next 6 min (p.7 [83]; p.10 [86]). The 20+2 and 20-2 rotations were counterbalanced with the two patterns (p.10 [86]). The light flashed at 1, 4 or 7 Hz at about 1 lx, 60 s on and 60 s off (p.3 [79]; p.10 [86]). The rise came in the burst-firing phase and was strongest with the 20-2 rotation (p.7 [83]); it was compared with periods without the fields (p.3 [79]). This program pairs Thomas with 20+2 (20 down to 6 ms per coil) and burst-firing with 20-2 (20 up to 34 ms): one of the counterbalanced combinations, chosen by this project. It has no no-field block. The Thomas pattern plays from the 849-point patent table at 1 ms per point; the lab's file had 859 points (Dotta & Persinger 2012 p.3 [74]). The burst-firing point values were never published, so the project's rising sweep stands in (230 points of 1 ms). Both repeat back to back, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2; the site names are this project's reading. One helmet delivers one of the two exposures. The lab drove both rings from one 286 computer (p.9 [85]); two helmets started by hand have no fixed phase relation. The paper gives 1 to 5 uT along the inside of each solenoid, 1 to 2 uT on average 'within the cross-sectional area' (p.10 [86]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT that is about 56 uT at the coil face and 24 uT at the scalp. 3 pairs, single lab, never independently replicated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Flashing light can trigger seizures in susceptible people. Do not use results for decisions about real people. Nobody with epilepsy, a seizure history or photosensitivity should take part in either role.
setting: Partner A (light): closed, quiet room, helmet on, in a diffuse light of about 1 lux flashing at 1, 4 or 7 Hz, 60 s on and 60 s off. Partner B: blindfolded in a dark room 10 m away, second helmet running this program; the lab counted photons 15 cm from the right side of B's head. A test that needs no photomultiplier (a project addition): B calls out whenever light seems to appear and a helper logs the times; A starts the trains at irregular times from a hidden list, compared with B's log only afterwards.
schedule: One session per pair. As a control, repeat on another day with the light covered or both helmets on sham (set by a helper, the same for both) and compare B's hit rates blind.
source: Dotta, Buckner, Lafrenie & Persinger 2011, Brain Res 1388:77-88 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21396353/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, Theoretical and experimental evidence of macroscopic entanglement between human brain activity and photon emissions, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Dotta & Persinger 2012, "Doubling" of local photon emissions when two simultaneous, spatially-separated, chemiluminescent reactions share the same magnetic field configurations, J Biophys Chem 3:72-80 (859- and 230-point patterns at 1 ms; primer/effector order) https://file.scirp.org/Html/17181.html ; Lehman 2016, PhD thesis, Laurentian University ("20-2" = 20, 22 ... 34 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/e7b03302-1b7f-4f4f-acf5-bdf41ee5370f/content ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Juden-Kelly, Dotta, Vares & Persinger 2015, JCER 6(9):728-737 (Burst-X: 230 points) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/497 ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University (230-point burst-firing file) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
